literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the same construct: full-length P-selectin with eGFP fused at its C-terminus ('P-selectin-eGFP'). P-selectin is a Type I single-pass transmembrane protein: signal peptide 1–41, extracellular ectodomain 42–773, TM 774–794, intracellular tail 795–830. A C-terminal fusion therefore places eGFP on the INTRACELLULAR face (after residue 830), not the extracellular surface. The papers confirm that the full-length tagged protein is trafficked to and displayed on the plasma membrane (the ectodomain is extracellular), but the eGFP tag itself is cytoplasmic. Per the instructions, a tag on an intracellular terminus without an explicit validated snorkel does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. No ledger line reports any tag insertion at the extracellular N-terminus (after signal cleavage at residue 41/42), in any extracellular loop, or anywhere else on the ectodomain. The ledger therefore supports zero extracellular surface tag sites for SELP.

literature_other_positions.note: P-selectin-eGFP is a C-terminal fusion; the C-terminus of P-selectin (residues 795–830) is intracellular, so eGFP is on the cytoplasmic face, not the extracellular surface.
